gap: The section teaches inter-rater agreement entirely as a thought experiment ('imagine a colleague applying your definitions') and never names the discipline's actual reliability tooling (percent agreement; chance-corrected Cohen's kappa). Learners leave able to assert agreement but with no vocabulary for the field's standard, weakening transfer to any coding study they read or run.
proposed_change: Add one short callout (or 2-3 sentences in Core Concept principle three / after Decision Rule check 3 'Agreement') naming percent agreement as the simplest check (raters agree on N of M coded turns) and noting that formal studies report a chance-corrected statistic (Cohen's kappa) because two raters can agree by luck on a small code set. Keep it light: the 'imagine a colleague' move is the practical floor for a single teacher (a definition tight enough that agreement is predictable, not a kappa computation); the callout just supplies the named ceiling so the term is not foreign in the literature.
